related_questions.question: What helps COVID symptoms go away faster?

text_blocks.snippet: While there's no magic cure to make COVID-19 symptoms disappear instantly, certain measures can help manage symptoms and potentially speed up recovery. These include getting plenty of rest, staying hydrated, and using over-the-counter medications for fever and aches. It's also important to monitor your health, isolate yourself to prevent spread, and contact a doctor immediately if you experience severe symptoms.
snippet_highlighted_words: getting plenty of rest, staying hydrated, and using over-the-counter medications for fever and aches

list.title: Rest:
list.snippet: Adequate sleep is crucial for the body's recovery process. Aim for more sleep than your usual routine.

list.title: Hydration:
list.snippet: Drinking plenty of fluids, especially water, helps to thin mucus and prevent dehydration, which can worsen symptoms.

list.title: Over-the-counter medications:
list.snippet: Fever reducers like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help manage fever and body aches.

list.title: Self-isolation:
list.snippet: To prevent the spread of the virus, isolate yourself from others and avoid close contact with people you live with. This includes using separate dishes, towels, and bedding.

list.title: Monitoring:
list.snippet: Regularly check your temperature and other symptoms to track the progression of the illness.

list.title: Medical advice:
list.snippet: Contact a doctor immediately if you experience severe symptoms or if your symptoms worsen.

related_questions.question: Can I go to work if my spouse has COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: It is generally recommended that you isolate at home and avoid going to work if your spouse has COVID-19. The CDC advises staying home and away from others, including household members who are not sick, if you have respiratory symptoms. This is to prevent the spread of the virus to others in your workplace and community.

related_questions.question: Am I still contagious after 7 days of COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, you could still be contagious after 7 days of COVID. While contagiousness generally peaks early in the illness and then wanes, most people are still contagious for an average of eight days. To determine if you are still contagious, it's recommended to stay isolated until you've been symptom-free for at least 24 hours and have not had a fever without the use of fever-reducing medication. If those conditions are met, then consider additional precautions like masking and hygiene practices for the following five days.

list.title: Factors Affecting Contagiousness:
list.snippet: Individual factors like underlying health conditions, severity of illness, and vaccination status can influence how long someone remains contagious.

list.title: CDC Recommendations:
list.snippet: The CDC recommends continued isolation until you have been symptom-free for 24 hours (without fever-reducing medication) and then additional precautions like masking and hygiene practices for at least five additional days.
